# PathQ-Former: Query-Based Fusion of Histology and Transcriptomics for Missing-Modality-Robust Cancer Survival Prediction

*Working draft, 2026-09-22. Target: NeurIPS 2026 workshop (4 pages + references). Numbers are final (REPORT.md); figure files are generated by `scripts/analyze_run.py` and `scripts/epoch_curves.py` and live in `paper/figures/`.*

**Sharoon Sharif**

## Abstract

Multimodal survival models that fuse whole-slide images (WSIs) with transcriptomics report gains over unimodal models, but they assume both modalities are present for every patient and are rarely compared with unimodal baselines under an identical training budget. We present PathQ-Former, a Q-Former-style architecture in which two banks of 32 learned queries read a patient's WSI patch embeddings and RNA-seq pathway tokens, and a small Transformer fuses the resulting 64 codes into discrete-time survival hazards. Absent modalities are replaced by learned null codes and dropped stochastically during training, and auxiliary unimodal survival heads force each branch to be prognostic on its own, so one checkpoint serves WSI+RNA, WSI-only and RNA-only patients. Under a single pre-registered protocol on five TCGA cohorts (SurvPath's patient-level 5-fold splits, disease-specific survival, fixed 20-epoch budget, three seeds, identical for all six methods), PathQ-Former improves the concordance index over the official SurvPath implementation by +0.037 pooled over 75 paired folds (paired t-test p = 0.002; Wilcoxon p = 0.005), with significant gains on BLCA and BRCA and ties elsewhere, and reproduces the gain on overall survival (+0.034, p = 0.003). It keeps a C-index of 0.54-0.67 with either modality removed, whereas SurvPath is unchanged without RNA and collapses to chance without WSI. It uses 20 % fewer parameters and trains 1.7x faster per step. We also report two negative results that we believe the field should state more often: the multimodal model is only within noise of a tuned RNA-only MLP pooled over cohorts, and joint fusion beats a late-fusion ensemble of its own two branches by only +0.01 (n.s.). A permutation test shows why the robustness differs: shuffling RNA across patients costs PathQ-Former 0.023 C-index and SurvPath nothing. Code, configurations, archived results and checkpoints are released.

## 1 Introduction

Prognosis from routine pathology and molecular profiling is a natural multimodal problem: histology captures tissue architecture and the tumour micro-environment, transcriptomics captures pathway activity, and the two are complementary in principle. Recent work fuses them with co-attention between WSI patch features and gene-set embeddings (MCAT [1], SurvPath [2], MMP [3]) and reports improvements over unimodal models on TCGA cohorts. Three practical problems remain.

First, **completeness is assumed.** In clinical practice one of the two modalities is frequently missing, most often sequencing. Co-attention architectures cannot run with a modality absent, and re-training per modality pattern is not a solution.

Second, **the comparison is often not budget-matched.** Multimodal models are compared with baselines trained under different schedules or selected on the validation set, and rarely with a strong unimodal transcriptomic baseline at equal budget.

Third, **event counts are tiny.** TCGA cohorts have 5-45 disease-specific events per validation fold. We show that the common practice of early stopping on validation loss is unreliable in this regime, degrading every method, and that a fixed epoch budget with the final checkpoint is the protocol under which published baselines reproduce their published numbers.

We address the first problem with an architecture and the other two with a protocol. Our contributions:

1. **PathQ-Former**, a query-based fusion model whose per-modality query banks make missing modalities a first-class case (learned null codes, per-sample modality dropout) and whose auxiliary unimodal heads balance the two branches. Its compute is independent of the number of patches.
2. **A budget-matched, seeded, pre-registered comparison** of six methods on five TCGA cohorts (180 five-fold runs), with paired statistics over (fold, seed) pairs, a mean-imputation missing-modality evaluation for baselines that cannot skip a modality, and a documented protocol audit.
3. **Results with their limits stated:** a significant gain over the strongest published multimodal baseline, robustness that the baseline lacks, and two honest negative findings (parity with an RNA-only MLP; fusion roughly equal to an ensemble) that bound what multimodal fusion currently buys on TCGA.

## 2 Related work

**Multimodal survival prediction.** MCAT [1] introduced genomic-guided co-attention between gene-set embeddings and WSI patches with a discrete-time survival loss [4]. SurvPath [2] replaced gene sets with biological pathway tokens and a memory-efficient patch-pathway co-attention; Porpoise [5] and MMP [3] explore late fusion and prototype-based fusion. All assume both modalities at test time. **Missing modalities.** Robustness of multimodal Transformers to absent inputs has been studied in vision-language [6] and medical imaging (shared-specific feature modelling [7]); we borrow the ideas of learned placeholder tokens and modality dropout. **Query-based fusion.** Learned queries that read a variable-length input through cross-attention (Perceiver [8], BLIP-2's Q-Former [9]) give a fixed-size, input-length-independent representation; PathQ-Former applies this per modality and fuses the query outputs. **Features.** We use frozen UNI2-h patch embeddings [10]; all baselines see the same features.

## 3 Method

### 3.1 Inputs
A patient is represented by (i) the concatenated patch embeddings of all their slides, X_h in R^{N x 1536} (N from 1k to 40k), and (ii) 275 pathway tokens built from 4,999 genes: each Reactome or Hallmark pathway with 3-300 member genes has a two-layer MLP over its members (hidden 128), as in SurvPath [2], giving X_g in R^{275 x d}. Genes are MinMax-scaled to [-1, 1] with statistics of the training fold.

### 3.2 Modality query blocks
Each modality m in {h, g} has K = 32 learned queries Q_m in R^{K x d}, d = 256. A query block applies, twice, pre-norm cross-attention from the queries to the (LayerNormed, linearly projected) modality tokens, self-attention among the queries and a feed-forward layer, producing Z_m in R^{K x d}. Cost is O(K N) in the patch count, so a 40k-patch patient costs the same as a 4k-patch one after the projection.

### 3.3 Null codes, modality dropout and fusion
A learned null code N_m in R^{K x d} per modality replaces Z_m whenever modality m is absent. During training each present modality is dropped per sample with probability p = 0.15, never both. The fusion Transformer (2 layers, d = 256) reads [Z_h ; Z_g] in R^{2K x d}; attention pooling yields a patient vector and a linear head outputs logits for 4 hazard bins whose edges are the quartiles of uncensored training event times.

### 3.4 Auxiliary unimodal heads
Without further constraints the fused head can learn to rely on the more informative branch, and the missing-modality behaviour becomes one-sided (Section 5.3). We add a survival head on Z_h and one on Z_g, trained with the same loss on the samples where the respective modality is present, weighted 0.5. They are discarded at inference.

### 3.5 Objective and risk
We use the discrete-time negative log-likelihood of [4] over the 4 bins (alpha = 0 for PathQ-Former, 0.5 for SurvPath as published) and rank patients by risk = -sum_t S(t), following MCAT/SurvPath. Training: RAdam, learning rate 1e-4, weight decay 1e-4, one warm-up epoch then cosine decay, batch size one patient with two-step gradient accumulation, dropout 0.25, class-balanced (bin, censorship) sampling, 20 epochs, final checkpoint. The full model has 16.9 M parameters including the pathway tokenizer.

## 4 Experimental setup

**Data.** Five TCGA cohorts with UNI2-h features and SurvPath's RNA and clinical tables: BLCA (359 patients, 113 disease-specific events), BRCA (868, 60), COADREAD (296, 37), HNSC (392, 117), STAD (318, 84). Splits are SurvPath's 5-fold patient-level splits; the endpoint is disease-specific survival (DSS), with overall survival (OS) as a secondary experiment.

**Protocol (identical for every method).** Bins from uncensored training patients; gene scaler fit on the training fold; fixed 20-epoch budget, final checkpoint; seeds 0, 1, 2 per cell; Harrell's C-index on continuous time as the primary metric (Uno's IPCW C, Brier/IBS and td-AUC are stored). Statistics: paired t and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests over (fold, seed) pairs, per cohort (15 pairs) and pooled (75 pairs). Spread in tables is the std over seeds of the 5-fold mean.

**Baselines.** The official SurvPath code [2] on the same 275 pathways and 4,096-patch subsample; ABMIL [11] on WSI only; SNN [12] and a two-layer MLP on the 4,999 genes; and a late-fusion ensemble (z-scored risk average) of a WSI-only and an RNA-only PathQ-Former. Baseline hyper-parameters follow the SurvPath repository.

**Missing-modality evaluation.** The same checkpoint is evaluated with WSI only, with RNA only, and with 10-50 % of validation patients randomly missing one modality (5 repeats). Baselines that cannot skip a modality receive the training-mean gene vector or mean patch instead, so the comparison measures degradation rather than availability.

**Why a fixed budget.** In a first campaign with early stopping on validation loss, every method including SurvPath and the RNA baselines landed near chance (0.45-0.55) on STAD, HNSC and BRCA: with 7-16 events per fold the validation NLL is noise and selection picked epoch 1-3 checkpoints while the validation C-index was still rising. Under a fixed budget SurvPath reproduces its published range and is seed-stable (BLCA 0.588/0.585/0.593; STAD 0.609/0.593/0.617). The budget was fixed at 20 epochs after pooled per-epoch curves showed PathQ-Former still improving at epoch 10 while SurvPath plateaued from epoch 8; the pre-registered choice is symmetric and the conclusions also hold at 10 epochs (+0.028 pooled, p = 0.034).

## 5 Results

### 5.1 Main comparison

**Table 1.** DSS C-index (mean +- std over 3 seeds of the 5-fold mean), fixed 20-epoch budget, final checkpoint. Pooled delta: paired over 75 (fold, seed) pairs.

| Method | Inputs | BLCA | BRCA | COADREAD | HNSC | STAD | Delta vs SurvPath, pooled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PathQ-Former | WSI+RNA | 0.609 +- .016 | 0.611 +- .039 | **0.638 +- .031** | 0.575 +- .012 | **0.593 +- .015** | **+0.037** (t p .002, W p .005) |
| PathQ-Former + aux | WSI+RNA | **0.630 +- .010** | 0.622 +- .033 | 0.613 +- .023 | **0.582 +- .025** | 0.572 +- .022 | **+0.036** (t p .007, W p .002) |
| SurvPath [2] | WSI+RNA | 0.594 +- .012 | 0.536 +- .026 | 0.570 +- .038 | 0.552 +- .019 | 0.587 +- .008 | reference |
| ABMIL [11] | WSI | 0.566 +- .011 | 0.575 +- .004 | 0.587 +- .023 | 0.562 +- .028 | 0.553 +- .020 | +0.001 (n.s.) |
| SNN [12] | RNA | 0.590 +- .009 | 0.558 +- .013 | 0.572 +- .028 | 0.535 +- .006 | 0.549 +- .009 | -0.007 (n.s.) |
| MLP | RNA | 0.611 +- .012 | **0.627 +- .013** | 0.633 +- .016 | 0.555 +- .012 | 0.532 +- .009 | +0.024 (t p .15, W p .30) |

PathQ-Former is at least as good as SurvPath on every cohort and significantly better on BLCA (+aux: +0.036, p = 0.024) and BRCA (+0.086, p = 0.004); COADREAD (+0.044 to +0.068), HNSC (+0.023 to +0.031) and STAD (-0.015 to +0.006) are within noise at 15 pairs. No single-modality baseline is significantly different from SurvPath pooled.

### 5.2 Against the strongest unimodal model
The RNA-only MLP is the strongest baseline. Pooled over 75 pairs PathQ-Former is +0.014 (p = 0.25) and PathQ-Former + aux +0.012 (p = 0.28) above it; SurvPath is -0.024 below it. Per cohort the multimodal model is never significantly worse than the MLP and is +0.04 to +0.06 better on STAD, where RNA alone is weak (MLP 0.532); the MLP in turn loses STAD and HNSC, and ABMIL loses BLCA and BRCA. The multimodal model is the only one that matches the best unimodal model on all five cohorts, but on TCGA at this sample size it does not beat it.

### 5.3 Missing modalities

**Table 2.** One modality removed at test time (20 epochs, seed 0, same checkpoint). Baselines receive training-mean imputation.

| Cohort | SurvPath full | no RNA | no WSI | PathQ+aux full | no RNA | no WSI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BLCA | 0.606 | 0.608 | 0.509 | 0.625 | 0.598 | 0.588 |
| BRCA | 0.552 | 0.552 | 0.514 | 0.647 | 0.610 | 0.671 |
| COADREAD | 0.532 | 0.534 | 0.480 | 0.595 | 0.547 | 0.594 |
| HNSC | 0.531 | 0.533 | 0.551 | 0.603 | 0.604 | 0.575 |
| STAD | 0.589 | 0.590 | 0.462 | 0.559 | 0.579 | 0.541 |

SurvPath's score is unchanged (max 0.002) when its RNA input is replaced by the training mean and falls to chance without WSI: its co-attention learns to route everything through histology. PathQ-Former + aux degrades gracefully in both directions and sometimes not at all. The auxiliary heads are the mechanism: without them the plain model is one-sided like SurvPath (BLCA WSI-only 0.635, RNA-only 0.535; HNSC 0.585 / 0.548) whereas with them it is balanced (0.598 / 0.588; 0.604 / 0.575), at no cost to the fused score (+0.02 on BLCA, p = 0.85). With 10-50 % of patients randomly missing one modality the fused C-index moves by at most 0.025 on any cohort over three seeds (Figure 2).

**Permutation test (three seeds).** Scoring each validation patient with another patient's RNA changes SurvPath's C-index by +0.001 (75 pairs, p = 0.43) and PathQ-Former + aux's by -0.023 (p = 0.016; seed-averaged p = 0.075); permuting WSI costs both models about 0.067 (p < 1e-3). SurvPath's co-attention therefore ignores the genomic branch, whereas PathQ-Former's fused prediction is histology-led but draws roughly a third of its WSI contribution from RNA. For the same PathQ checkpoints the learned null codes are at least as good as mean imputation (RNA-only 0.579 vs 0.569, WSI-only 0.591 vs 0.595), so the robustness comes from the balanced branches, not from the placeholder itself.

### 5.4 Is fusion more than an ensemble?
With two seeds of the single-modality models (50 pairs), joint fusion is +0.011 over a late-fusion ensemble of the WSI-only and RNA-only PathQ-Formers (t p = 0.39; seed-averaged +0.010, p = 0.32; ensemble C-index BLCA 0.629, BRCA 0.606, COADREAD 0.620, HNSC 0.571, STAD 0.544), and the ensemble itself is +0.027 over SurvPath (n.s.). Joint fusion beats the better single branch by 0 to +0.03. On BLCA, none of the query count (16/32/64), fusion depth (1/2/3) or modality-dropout rate (0/0.15/0.3/0.5) moves the fused score outside one fold-std (0.60-0.64). We therefore claim a unified model, not a better fusion mechanism.

### 5.5 Overall survival
With OS as the endpoint (seed 0) PathQ-Former + aux vs SurvPath is BLCA 0.595 vs 0.552 (p = 0.008), BRCA 0.596 vs 0.523 (p = 0.015), COADREAD 0.581 vs 0.596, HNSC 0.536 vs 0.510 (p = 0.046), STAD 0.603 vs 0.559; pooled +0.034 over 25 folds (t p = 0.003, W p = 0.003). Missing-modality behaviour is unchanged (BLCA 0.595 / 0.576 / 0.592 for both / WSI-only / RNA-only).

### 5.6 Ablations of the final configuration (BLCA, seed 0)
Hazard bins: 2 -> 0.628, 4 -> 0.625 (3-seed 0.630), 8 -> 0.609. Pathway sets: Reactome+Hallmark (275) 0.630, Xena (281) 0.628, Hallmark-only (50) 0.600. Training on a 4,096-patch subsample instead of all patches: 0.626 vs 0.625, so the gain over SurvPath is not explained by seeing more patches.

### 5.7 Efficiency
On an RTX PRO 4000 with real BLCA patients (median 6,214 patches): PathQ-Former 16.9 M parameters, 35.0 ms forward, 104 ms forward+backward, 1.17 GiB peak memory on all patches (34.7 / 104.1 ms / 0.17 GiB at 4,096 patches); SurvPath 21.2 M, 35.7 / 175.6 ms / 0.20 GiB at 4,096 patches and 36.0 / 176.0 ms / 1.74 GiB on all patches. PathQ-Former's step is 1.7x faster and flat in the patch count.

## 6 Discussion and limitations

**What the evidence supports.** A budget-matched, seeded gain over the strongest published multimodal baseline that survives two paired tests and a second endpoint; a robustness property the baseline structurally lacks; and stability to the budget, bin count, pathway set and patch budget.

**What it does not.** (i) The multimodal model is not significantly better than a tuned RNA-only MLP pooled over cohorts and loses to it within noise on BRCA and COADREAD; TCGA transcriptomics is a strong prognostic signal and multimodal papers should report this baseline at equal budget. (ii) Fusion is worth roughly an ensemble of its branches (+0.01 with two seeds), and the fused prediction is histology-led (permuting WSI costs 0.067, permuting RNA 0.023). (iii) Per-cohort significance exists only for BLCA and BRCA; COADREAD (37 events) and STAD are inconclusive at this sample size; OS uses one seed and the single-modality and ensemble experiments two. (iv) Missingness is simulated as random or complete removal, not informative missingness. (v) TCGA only; frozen UNI2-h features; no external validation. (vi) The comparison with SurvPath is against its official code under our protocol, not against its published numbers (OS, different preprocessing).

**A protocol finding.** Early stopping on validation loss with 7-16 events per fold selected epoch 1-3 checkpoints for every method and produced near-chance multimodal and unimodal results on three cohorts. Several published comparisons on event-poor cohorts use this practice. We recommend fixed budgets, final checkpoints, seeds, and paired statistics over (fold, seed) pairs, and we release every run so the analysis can be repeated.

## 7 Conclusion
PathQ-Former turns missing modalities into a first-class case of multimodal survival modelling with a query-based design whose cost is independent of slide size. Under a strict protocol it significantly outperforms the strongest published multimodal baseline and, unlike it, keeps working with either modality absent, while its parity with an RNA-only MLP and its ensemble-level fusion gain mark the current limits of multimodal fusion on TCGA. Code, configurations, all 180 run results and the checkpoints are public.

## Reproducibility statement
Code: https://github.com/SharoonSharif/PathQFormer (MIT), archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22900123. `scripts/reproduce_tables.sh` regenerates every table from the archived per-run results in one minute; each Table 1 cell is one documented command; checkpoints are on the HuggingFace Hub (`sharoonsharif1/PathQFormer-checkpoints`). Data access: SurvPath repository (splits, RNA, pathways) and the gated UNI2-h features.
